title: Ozone and moisture gave no clear repeated link to plant sample size in four eastern US forest samples in 1994-2010
abstract: We tested whether annual ozone and soil moisture variation was linked to the number of plants examined for visible ozone injury. We used 5,277 site-years from Northeast and North Central US samples in 1994-2002 and 2003-2010. Models separated annual products from products with site means and controlled for site, year, exposure curves, temperature, visit date and survey categories. Four joint log-count slopes ranged from -0.041 to -0.00002 per 10 ppm-h ozone per moisture SD. All ordinary and four-test cluster intervals included zero. An exact split into sampled species and plants per species gave no clear repeated secondary link. A close-monitor check gave an isolated negative slope in the early Northeast. Few clusters, negative secondary variance estimates, selected completed visits and estimated exposure limit inference. This is a test of the observation process, not a causal injury or biodiversity-loss test. Counts matched the archived FIA source. The package gives code, aggregate moments, exact external-source hashes and reproduction instructions.

display.caption: Joint ozone and moisture slopes for log examined plants, examined species and plants per species in four region-period samples. All four main intervals cross zero. Thick lines show ordinary 95 percent intervals; thin lines show four-test intervals. The two right panels are secondary. Two negative secondary variances have no interval.

citations.reason: Exact verified external analysis panel and archived FIA count table. Underlying field records overlap. We test sampling counts as outcomes.
Annual product decomposition and regional-period design motivate this distinct test of plant sample size.
Earlier fixed-effort injury test motivates examining the count process directly.
Earlier fixed-species injury comparison; this study separates count slopes for examined species and plants per species.
